# Chrome border widths: snapping, per side, separate and collapsed tables, margin boxes, Scale 1 and 0.9 (M3-14 probe)
# Source: tmp/m3probe/borders.html (kind dom) and borders_pdf.py (kinds pdf-*) (dev-only probe page, never committed to Go code), 2026-11-24, run by tmp/m3probe/run.sh: chromium --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --dump-dom,
# as Chromium 156.0.8078.73 built on Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) (headless, getBoundingClientRect). Units: CSS px (pdf kinds: CSS px of the drawn border).
# Format: kind "dom": {"name","w" (container width, CSS px),"css","html"} reproduce the case; every rect is [x,y,w,h] of the border box relative to the case container (a display:flow-root div at the page origin, margin 0), 3 decimals (Blink LayoutUnit = 1/64 px); "m" border boxes by key (key ending [] = all matches in tree order), "t" first client rect of the element text (Range), "cs" computed style values (pseudo-elements are read with getComputedStyle(el, "::x")), "m0" the same rects as "m" with every transform neutralised, "x" extra values. The first line {"meta":...} gives the viewport (innerWidth, innerHeight = A4 794x1123 CSS px). "cs".a / .f / .td0 = computed border-*-width (the snapped used value); kind "pdf-box": a uniform solid border of that width drawn in a PDF printed at Scale scale (stroke width read with pdftocairo -svg); kind "pdf-margin-box": a @top-center border-bottom and a @bottom-left border of that width (named pages, page margins 25/20/22mm) as drawn.
# Rule: a border width is snapped at computed-value time: width >= 1px -> floor(px) (1.99px -> 1px, 2.5pt = 3.33px -> 3px, 3mm = 11.34px -> 11px, 4.5px -> 4px); 0 < width < 1px -> 1px (0.1px, 0.3px, 0.5pt, 1e-5px all 1px); 0 -> 0; keywords thin 1px, medium 3px, thick 5px; negative -> invalid (no border).
# The drawn width is the computed one, identical at Scale 1 and 0.9 (not scaled before snapping); margin-box borders follow the same rule and are not affected by Scale (same drawn size at both scales).
# Collapsed tables use the snapped widths with half-widths on each side of the grid line (3px/5px neighbours: cell edges at 1.5 and 2.5).
# css zoom != 1 is only here as a curiosity: computed values are unzoomed fractions (0.5pt at zoom 0.9 -> 1.11111px).
